title: A context-cost audit argues persistent agents should cache information by change rate
friendlyTitle: Stop making your AI agent pay to reread the same instructions
summary: An engineering write-up separates an agent’s context into layers that change at different speeds, from stable identity and instructions to live task state. The author reports cutting input costs by roughly 85% by caching stable prefixes instead of repeatedly sending the agent’s full personality and background.
friendlySummary: The author split agent context into stable and changing parts, then cached the stable parts. They report reducing input costs by about 85%.
whyItMatters: Always-on agents can quietly spend most of their budget rereading unchanged context. Structuring prompts for provider caching and isolating frequently changing state can reduce cost and latency without removing useful instructions.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Long-running agents can become much cheaper when they do not resend the same background on every call. Put stable instructions first and changing task details later.
